name: Cyient Ltd
title: Cyient Ltd - 532175 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Cyient to acquire TAO Digital for $218M total (upfront ~$130M, 7.9x CY25 EBITDA), all-cash, mostly debt-funded, EPS-accretive after ~1.5 years.
summary.overview: Cyient announced the acquisition of TAO Digital on a short-notice investor call held 1 June 2026, not a regular Q4 FY26 results call. Total deal value is $218M, of which about $130M is paid upfront at closing for 100% of shares, with the balance linked to two earnout tranches over two years tied to EBITDA growth. Management framed the deal as a shift from pure-play ER&D toward life-cycle engineering that combines engineering with data, software and AI, and a move from project work to multi-year annuity deals. Management gave limited financial disclosure: no TAO revenue or EBITDA figures beyond the multiple, and no margin or growth guidance beyond the CY27 target discussed in Q&A.

financial_highlights.value: Less than 5% of overall deal value, paid only on achieving outcomes

financial_highlights.metric: Target EBITDA margin (as stated by management)

segments.name: TAO Digital: data digitization / data conversion
segments.commentary: Roughly 20% of TAO's business and about 40% of its workforce, mostly offshore; management said this lowers the consolidated billing rate and revenue per employee (about $33-34k per Sandeep Shah's calculation).

segments.name: TAO Digital: core high-end business (the other ~80%)
segments.commentary: Management said this is the value driver and comprises platform engineering (next-gen modular, composable platforms), high-end data engineering (data lake houses, warehouses, private AI infrastructure) and software/AI platform engineering, with billing rates described as high.

guidance_outlook: Upfront ~$130M paid at closing for 100% of shares; two earnout tranches over two years post-closing based on EBITDA growth, with an accelerator linked to synergy EBITDA.
Deal is all-cash and EPS-accretive after amortisation, integration costs and debt interest; management expects it to become substantially accretive after roughly 1.5 years of integration.
Acquisition primarily debt-funded, with a large part of the debt to be serviced from the target's free cash flow; ROCE-positive.

Growth assumptions described as conservative: TAO's historical growth above 100% CAGR; model applies roughly 20% growth and holds EBITDA margin around 20%, with a haircut in year 2 for integration costs.
Management indicated a non-recurring charge in the current quarter from this transaction, smaller than the prior quarter's charge, which related to a different transaction that has been paused.
Cross-sell into Cyient accounts is the key synergy; expected to build momentum in years 2 and 3 rather than contribute significantly to near-term EBITDA.
Management intends to retain TAO's key management beyond the two-year earnout.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or utilisation figures were discussed for the target or Cyient.
Management described the target as a platform-level acquisition rather than a bolt-on.
demand_pricing: Management cited the TAM expanding from a ~$100B ER&D outsourcing market to an estimated ~$2 trillion across Cyient's existing industries (aerospace, energy, med tech, etc.) without entering new industries.
Customer CSAT feedback: 79 of 116 executives polled (about 70%) asked for more software, data and AI capabilities for two consecutive years.

Customer growth expected from volume growth in assets and products in aerospace, energy and med tech, plus services revenue; outcome-based commercial models under active discussion with several customers.
Data collection and digitization described as a wedge with a 2-3 year runway; management said data volumes are doubling every quarter.
Management said the business model may shift from headcount and hours to volume of data digitized, but this has not happened yet.
Buying centres are multiple: R&D, CDO, CIO, supply chain, services and business units; CIO remains important in some accounts.
Customer concentration is said to be low; top 10 customers about 60% of revenue (approximate, from Q&A); TAO has several high single-digit million-dollar accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Is building IT-type capabilities a focus, and who are the competitors for annuity deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukamal Banerjee said the boundary between IT and engineering is blurring, accelerated by AI, and that the work remains an engineering problem tied to the product life cycle rather than back-office IT. No competitor was named in the response.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue growth and EBITDA margins; organic versus inorganic growth history.
qa_highlights.answer: Shrinivas Kulkarni said the growth assumed is conservative relative to TAO's history of more than 100% growth over three years. Sukamal Banerjee said organic growth has been over 100% CAGR from a small base; no margin expansion is assumed in the model.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue per employee of $33-34k and current EBITDA margin versus the 16-17% CY27 target.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the low billing rate reflects the offshore mix and the data digitization segment. Kulkarni said margins are closer to 20%, with a haircut applied for integration costs over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the nonrecurring charge in Q4 linked to this deal, and are more deals in the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Kulkarni said the Q4 charge was unrelated, that there are other opportunities in the pipeline in early stages, and that this quarter will carry a smaller non-recurring charge from this deal.

qa_highlights.question: Will the buying centre change for existing engineering clients, and EPS accretion basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukamal Banerjee said there are multiple buying centres, with the CIO still important in some accounts. Kulkarni confirmed EPS accretion after amortisation, integration costs and debt interest.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of management incentive/retention, client concentration, and cross-sell/upsell.
qa_highlights.answer: Kulkarni said the incentive is below 5% of deal value and paid only on outcomes. Management said cross-sell into Cyient accounts is the priority and will take time, with year 2-3 momentum; no single customer concentration risk; top 10 about 60% (approximate).

risks_watch: Debt-funded deal: track the debt quantum, interest cost, and how much is serviced from the target's free cash flow.
Earnout dependence on EBITDA growth and synergy targets; watch disclosure of TAO revenue and EBITDA in subsequent filings.
Integration costs and the non-recurring charge in the coming quarter; EPS accretion timing of about 1.5 years.
Margin gap: management cites ~20% EBITDA, but the data digitization (~20% of business) has low billing rates and may dilute blended margins.
Cross-sell into Cyient accounts depends on buying-centre navigation (CIO versus R&D) and management retention beyond two years.
Automation of data work could compress volume-based revenue in the digitization business, though management says the model has not shifted yet.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on strategy and the AI-driven convergence thesis, but more guarded on numbers: Shrinivas Kulkarni repeatedly relied on "conservative" assumptions and the SEBI disclosure, and gave few direct figures for TAO's revenue, margin or client mix.
key_quotes: The acquisition of TAO Digital marks a pivotal moment in how our business is evolving.
So the answer is there are multiple buying centers. There are increasingly these new buying centers, which are emerging.
This is an all -cash deal that is EPS accretive for us, also ROCE positive and the company will be wholly -owned subsidiary of Cyient.
the value we are focused on is the other 80% of the business, and that's the driver for this acquisition.
